articles.title: Prisoners freed early in England and Wales risk living on the streets, say probation officers
articles.summary:
Warning of a lack of hostel places for 2,000 criminals due to be released over the next month to ease overcrowding

Hundreds of prisoners are due to be released early from jail on Thursday…

blocks.text: Hundreds of prisoners are due to be released early from jail on Thursday amid warnings that many will have nowhere to live and the probation system will struggle to monitor them.

About 2,000 criminals including domestic abusers and violent offenders are to be freed over the next month, with another 3,000 in stages over the next year to ease overcrowding. The number was reduced from 6,000 after an intervention by the prime minister, Andy Burnham.
Prisoners are supposed to be found appropriate accommodation before their release, significantly reducing reoffending rates.
But a probation source told the Guardian that their colleagues in some towns and cities were struggling to find hostel places.
“We have a handful of places for ex-offenders and they are full. We are now looking at releasing some people straight on to the street,” the source said.

Enver Solomon, the chief executive of the social justice charity Nacro, said: “We know that leaving prison homeless can put people on a path back into custody. It is vital that the whole system from prisons and probation to councils and community providers work together to give people a roof over their heads.”

Napo, the probation officers’ union, has raised the issue of the accommodation shortage with prison bosses. The task of finding beds for prisoners is expected to reach critical levels from 13 October, when a second tranche of prisoners is due for release.
Ben Cockburn, the union’s national chair, said HM Prison Service seemed to be in “absolute denial” about the state of the Probation Service.
“We have massive staff shortages, unsustainable and dangerously high workloads and electronic monitoring is failing to deliver,” he said.

Ministers say the expanded early release scheme is needed to prevent the collapse of the criminal justice system. They say the Conservatives in their time in power added too few prison places while increasing the length of sentences.

Criminals will be excluded from the scheme if they have been jailed in child grooming gang cases or convicted of indecent assault. Those guilty of manslaughter will also be excluded, meaning the killers of Andrew Harper, a police officer who died in the line of duty in 2019, will not be eligible.
The releases will take place across dozens of prisons across England and Wales from Thursday.

The expansion of the scheme is happening as a result of the 2026 Sentencing Act, which allows ministers to reduce the point at which certain prisoners can be freed from 40% of a fixed-term sentence to a third.
Several hundred people are likely to be released on 1 October as part of the first phase of the expanded scheme, with more to follow in subsequent months.
after newsletter promotion

The Ministry of Justice says it is launching the biggest ever expansion of electronic monitoring, with a new presumption that offenders will be electronically tagged and monitored when they leave prison.

But a report released this week by probation and police watchdogs warned that some criminals were waiting up to five months to be fitted with a tag, leading to repeated breaches of court and prison orders.
Only 55% of GPS and radio frequency tags were fitted on time, according to the report’s findings. The figure was 60% for alcohol monitoring tags.

Keir Starmer’s government launched an early release scheme in September 2024, months after the general election. Images of prisoners swigging champagne, being driven away in sports cars and thanking the then prime minister were seized upon by the government’s critics.

Figures show the number of people behind bars has jumped by more than 1,700 in the past three months. The prison population of England and Wales stood at 87,499 on Monday, according to weekly government data.
A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “This government inherited prisons on the brink of collapse and a homelessness crisis, with rough sleeping more than doubling since 2010.

“We’re pulling every lever to fix this, building 14,000 new prison places and working with councils and charities to halve prison leaver homelessness by 2029, supported by a record £700m investment in probation and community services.”

articles.title: Healey urged to offer energy support in budget as bills rise 4%
articles.summary:
Millions of people in Great Britain face increase from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home

John Healey is under growing pressure to offer fresh energy support for…
articles.byline: Heather Stewart, Richard Partington and Jillian Ambrose

blocks.text: John Healey is under growing pressure to offer fresh energy support for households in next month’s budget as millions face a 4% rise in charges from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home.

In his speech at Labour’s conference in Liverpool this week, the chancellor warned that the government had limited resources to cushion the worldwide economic shocks hitting Britain, while arguing his budget would have fiscal discipline at its core.

The quarterly energy price cap, set by the regulator for Great Britain, Ofgem, will rise to its highest level in three years despite Andy Burnham’s decision to cut VAT from electricity bills to save the average household £45 a year from 1 October.
Households also face rising road fuel costs after diesel prices reached a record high of almost £2 a litre this week, which is expected to accelerate the rising cost of goods across the economy.
Treasury sources insist the 28 October budget will be tightly focused amid the challenging global backdrop, as bond market jitters add to the pressure on the public finances.
Insiders said tax devolution was likely to be centre stage to meet Andy Burnham’s promise to shake up Whitehall, while several big decisions could be pushed back to a spending review next year.

Some MPs are privately concerned that Healey and his team have failed to grasp the severity of the energy crunch ahead. “Without it [fresh energy support], the vibes will end,” said one Labour MP. “The problem is the Treasury are just not understanding where the country are.”
Healey warned in his speech that the money New Labour had in the 1990s was “simply not there now”, although he also vowed to offer “a bit of breathing space” for households and businesses.

As energy bills rise for millions of households from Thursday, a group of leading campaigners, charities, trade unions and thinktanks warned that failure to take action would risk deepening the cost of living crisis.

Writing in an open letter to the chancellor and the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, the group – including the New Economics Foundation, the Joseph Rowntree Foundation and Generation Rent – called for a package of universal energy support as well as targeted measures to help those most in need.

Coordinated by the Cost of Living Action campaign group, other signatories included Neal Lawson of Compass and Mathew Lawrence of Common Wealth – both of whose ideas have fed into Burnham’s policymaking.

blocks.caption: Cornwall Insight predicts the energy price cap will increase by a further 16% from January to £1,999 for the average annual dual-fuel bill. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian

blocks.text: With the war in the Middle East pushing up global oil and gas prices, the leading energy forecaster Cornwall Insight predicts the cap will increase by a further 16% from January to £1,999 for the average annual dual-fuel bill.
Paul Nowak, the general secretary of the TUC, said this “energy bill emergency” meant the government should “go further and faster” at the budget to protect households.
On Wednesday, Burnham said Labour “will do our best” but warned that the government faced tough financial constraints, telling the BBC there was not “huge room for manoeuvre” to take further action.
In his first weeks in office, the prime minister announced the six-month VAT holiday on electricity bills and a £2 cap on bus fares in England.
after newsletter promotion
The Treasury is under pressure to extend the six-month VAT holiday, and shift the levies used to support new clean energy projects and grid upgrades from energy bills into general taxation.

The changes are understood to already be under consideration by Fahnbulleh, who is reportedly hoping to save customers an average of £120 a year on their energy bills – but this could involve putting up taxes by as much as £3bn.

However, the campaigners warned that further cost of living support was needed. “It is clear that this does not go far enough and that what is coming down the track this winter requires a much more substantial response,” they wrote.

Highlighting the risks from soaring energy bills, new polling carried out by More in Common on behalf of the Joseph Rowntree Foundation shows 28% of households are extremely worried about the prospect of the Iran war pushing up bills this winter, while 43% are quite concerned.
It found 66% of British adults think the government needs to do more to tackle the cost of energy.

Calling for bolder action, NEF urged the government to introduce a new “national energy guarantee” giving all households a basic amount of energy at a fixed low cost, with higher levels of consumption charged at market prices.
Responding to the letter, Fahnbulleh said:“I know energy price rises weigh heavily on homes across the UK this winter.

“From today, our VAT cut will give households some much-needed breathing space, making the energy price cap £45 a year less than it would have been. This follows the £150 of costs we removed from bills earlier this year.
“Alongside this, we continue to look at what more we can do to protect families from unaffordable bills, as we drive down bills for good through clean power.”
Burnham said: “For many families, the energy bill is the one they dread the most. I don’t accept that it has to be this way, and I am determined to bring down costs for good.”

Thus far, there is no evidence to show that the Vice President or the respondent has denied or is denying the SALN on record, not only before the Office of the Ombudsman but also before this Court,” Escudero said.

articles.title: Netanyahu says too early to tell who was behind plane incident as flydubai halts all flights to Israel
articles.summary:
Israeli prime minister cautions against early conclusions when asked if there were any signs of Iranian involvement

Benjamin Netanyahu has said it was too early to tell who was ultimately…

blocks.text: Benjamin Netanyahu has said it was too early to tell who was ultimately behind the apparent attempt to crash a ⁠Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, even as Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations called the incident a “terror attack”, without apportioning blame.

Danny Danon told Fox News on Wednesday night that Israel had “no doubt that it was a terror attack from a radical individual. We still cannot link it to a terror state or terror organisation, but for sure we know there was an intention to bring that plane down.”
Flydubai said its flights to and from Israel would be suspended while the investigation takes place and urged all parties “to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts”.

The incident – which began when one pilot stabbed another on the flight deck in an apparent attempt to take control of the aircraft – is under investigation. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had more than 170 people on board, most of them from Israel.

In what have been hailed as acts of tremendous bravery, several passenger rushed the cockpit of the flight and wrestled the controls from the alleged attacker even as the plane descended sharply, managing to eventually taking control and stabilising the plane before making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, told Fox News host Sean Hannity: “We’ll get to the root of ⁠this attacker, whether he had accomplices” but cautioned that it was “too early to say” when asked whether there was any indication of Iranian involvement.

The pilot accused of carrying out the stabbing was being questioned by Saudi authorities, the Israeli prime minister said, adding that he expected he would soon be taken to the UAE, where the flight took off from. Netanyahu said earlier that he had spoken with the UAE’s president, who agreed that Israel would join the interrogation of the suspect.
Israeli officials, speaking on condition of anonymity to reporters, said the attacker was an Omani national, but there was no comment from Oman or the UAE.

Israel’s foreign ministry later briefed its diplomats around the world that the incident was an “attempted terrorist attack against Israelis, the United Arab Emirates, and the Abraham Accords,” referring to the deal that normalised relations between the two countries in 2020.

But on Wednesday evening Donald Trump told reporters the incident remained unclear, after he had spoken to Netanyahu. “It seems as though the co-pilot was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack-job, and he stabbed the pilot,” the US president told reporters in the Oval Office.
Netanyahu was among the world leaders celebrating the bravery of the passengers and crew of the flydubai flight on Wednesday.
A video shared by the prime minister’s office showed passenger Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber, speaking to Netanyahu at length about how the events on board played out.

Hayoun told the prime minister how he and other passengers heard screaming and felt the air pressure change as the plane dived before they forced their way into the cockpit and found the attacker at the instrument panel.
“I grabbed the attacker, put him in a chokehold, and dragged him out first,” Hayoun said during the meeting with Netanyahu after the plane had landed safely and the passengers were flown to Israel.
As others wrestled with the attacker, Hayoun said he grabbed the controls and pulled them the way he had seen on television. Then other crew members took over.

The stabbed pilot was identified as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, who was said to have made the emergency call and opened the door to the cockpit, allowing others to rush in and subdue the attacker.

In a post on X early on Thursday, Indian prime minister Narendra Modi lauded Machchhar a “hero”. “In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously ‌injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy,” Modi ​said.
Machchhar, an Indian citizen from Mumbai, is being treated in a hospital in Saudi Arabia’s north-western city of Tabuk, where the plane landed safely.

articles.summary: Two provincial government officers appeared before the Senate impeachment court Thursday to shed light on the alleged properties of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio. One of…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 12:47pm
Two provincial government officers appeared before the Senate impeachment court Thursday to shed light on the alleged properties of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.
One of them was Marco Pineda, Deputy Register of Deeds III of the City of Samal.
Pineda was subpoenaed to testify about a property in Island Garden City of Samal registered in the name of Carpio.
He said that he is also "concurrently serving as an assisting register of deeds of Davao City."

“Kami po ang repositoryo ng lahat ng mga titulo at ari-arian, personal or real. Saka tungkulin namin na kung mayroong mga dokumentong sinusumite sa aming tanggapan, ito po ay aming tungkulin na suriin kung ito ay kumpleto,” said Pineda.
(We are the repository of all titles and properties, whether personal or real. It is also our duty to examine any documents submitted to our office to ensure they are complete.)
Pineda said that their office also has jurisdiction over Davao del Norte.
He said that he submitted documents related to the alleged property of Carpio in Samal.

The net worth of Duterte and her husband reached more than P98 million in 2025, an 11.46% increase from their 2024 net worth based on their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
GMA News Research found that the Duterte-Carpio couple declared a net worth of P98,656,131.20 in 2025. The net worth they declared in the prior year was P88 million.
On the other hand, their declared total assets were P122,797,727.20, which is a 24.72% increase from the P98 million in 2024. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution: Sara Duterte didn’t declare Mans Carpio’s 2 Davao properties in SALN
articles.summary: The two properties are worth around P9 million combined

blocks.text: COUPLE. Sara Duterte with her husband Manases "Mans" Carpio
Rappler file
The two properties are worth around P9 million combined

MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband Mans Carpio purchased two properties that cannot be found in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), the prosecution argued on Thursday, October 1.
Prosecutor Keith Flores handled the direct examination of two witnesses from the Land Registration Authority (LRA) to confirm the multi-million-peso properties in Davao Region sold to Carpio.
Davao City Register of Deeds IV Kathy Florence Baldonado said a lot in Matina, Davao City was sold to Carpio for P6 million in July 2024.
City of Samal Deputy Register of Deeds III Marco Pineda said Carpio also bought a property on the island for P3 million in 2018.
Both properties do not correspond to any entries in the Vice President’s SALN.
The prosecution wants Duterte removed from office for betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution in connection with her alleged unexplained wealth.

“We clearly mentioned in Article 2… that one of the allegations is that the Vice President failed to disclose in her SALNs all of her properties. And that’s impossible for us to have known of this property simply because it’s not disclosed in the SALN,” Flores said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PH adopts Phnom Penh Declaration vs. online scams
articles.summary: The Philippines has committed to working with Cambodia and other international partners to fight online scams and related transnational crimes as it adopted the Phnom Penh Declaration to eradicate…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 12:34pm

The Philippines has committed to working with Cambodia and other international partners to fight online scams and related transnational crimes as it adopted the Phnom Penh Declaration to eradicate the scourge.

The Phnom Penh Declaration outlines 11 commitments to strengthen collective action against online scams, including stronger international cooperation, dismantling criminal networks and online scam compounds, disrupting and recovering criminal proceeds, strengthening laws, and protecting victims of trafficking and vulnerable people.

At the International Conference on Combating Online Scams (ICCOS) in Phnom Penh, the delegation participated in high-level and panel discussions on national and international efforts to combat online scams during the two-day conference on September 23 and 24.
Department of Justice (DOJ) Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato attended the conference with other officials from the agency and the National Bureau of Investigation.

Dato underscored the need for stronger international cooperation in addressing the transnational nature of online scams, as he delivered a speech during the High-Level Session on "Online Scams as a Global Emergency."

He said Filipinos are both victims of online fraud and human trafficking into scam operations. The Justice official cited the Philippines' efforts to strengthen its laws and enforcement while protecting trafficking victims.

Dato also called for closer cross-border cooperation among law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, and financial intelligence units, particularly in preserving digital evidence and freezing and returning scam proceeds to victims. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution drops Trillanes as witness in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: No reason has been provided by the prosecution regarding its sudden change of heart

blocks.text: SONNY TRILLANES. File photo shows civil society group The Silent Majority along with former senator Antonio Trillanes file plunder and graft charges against Vice President Sara Duterte before the Office of the Ombudsman on January 21, 2026.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
No reason has been provided by the prosecution regarding its sudden change of heart
MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution withdrew its bid to present former senator Antonio Trillanes IV as its witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
The prosecution had intended to call Trillanes to the witness stand to testify on Duterte’s bank records.

“The prosecution has finally decided not to present former senator Sonny Trillanes. We seek the kind indulgence of the honorable impeachment court for the belated final position on this particular concern,” prosecutor Jinky Luistro told the court on Thursday, October 1.
No reason has been provided by the prosecution regarding its sudden change of heart.
Trillanes, back in 2016, leaked documents detailing years’ worth of bank transactions involving then-presidential aspirant Rodrigo Duterte and his family members.
During the impeachment proceedings at the House back in April, it was confirmed that the Dutertes’ transactions from Trillanes’ records matched with the AMLC records.

In total, the AMLC said there was a total of P6.7 billion in large and suspicious transactions that flowed through the bank accounts of Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio from 2006 to 2025. The amount is a huge disparity from the Vice President’s net worth, which peaked at over P90 million in 2025 based on her SALN.
More details to follow. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Who is prosecutor Keith Flores in Sara Duterte's impeachment trial?
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court resumed the hearing on Vice President Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth on Tuesday, after a strategic procedural pause the previous day.

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 12:11pm
The Senate impeachment court resumed the hearing on Vice President Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth on Tuesday, after a strategic procedural pause the previous day.
The impeachment trial continued with witnesses Davao City Register of Deeds IV Kathy Florence Baldonado and City of Samal Deputy Register of Deeds III Marco Pineda.

House prosecutor and Bukidnon 2nd District Rep. Keith Flores presented the title of a 379-square-meter property in Barangay Matina, Davao City, registered under the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio.
LIVE UPDATES: Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial (October 1, 2026)
The property was sold for P6 million in July 2024.
The title also shows an P8-million mortgage with Philippine Savings Bank, which was taken out in August 2024.

Flores also moved to reveal Duterte’s 2026 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), but Presiding Officer Francis Escudero pointed out that SALNs do not require officials to indicate the actual area of a property.
Who is Keith Flores?
Flores, Bukidnon's 2nd District since 2019, is a lawyer.
He was born in Agusan del Norte in April 1972.
Flores earned his law degree at Ateneo de Davao University and was admitted to the Philippine Bar in 2001.
He became a member of the Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats after taking his oath in 2023.
Flores is serving his third and final term as congressman after winning in the 2019, 2022, and 2025 elections.
Among the bills he authored are the Anti-Political Dynasty Act of 2025, the Anti-Online Gambling Promotion in E-Wallets Act, and the National Water Resources Management Act. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Israelis divided as vote that could oust Netanyahu only weeks away
articles.summary:
Some on streets of Jerusalem pledge their support to prime minister while others hope for change

On the streets of Jerusalem, crowded with secular and ultra-Orthodox Jews, religious…
articles.byline: Lorenzo Tondo and Quique Kierszenbaum in Jerusalem; graphics by Ana Lucía González Paz

blocks.text: On the streets of Jerusalem, crowded with secular and ultra-Orthodox Jews, religious nationalists, settlers, Palestinians, and soldiers returning from deployments, uncertainty hangs over an election less than a month away that could mark a turning point for a country profoundly changed after the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023 and nearly three years of war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The political battle remains on a knife-edge.
For over two years most polls have predicted that the coalition of parties led by prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu will collectively slip below the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government.

But there is no clear path to power for his main opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, the former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, even if he maintains current levels of support, because he has ruled out going into coalition with any of the parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, who are projected to claim a critical 12 seats.

For Netanyahu to stay in power, he would have to either put together a different coalition or pull off an unprecedented election night surprise. Another deeply fragmented Knesset seems likely, in which neither side is close to securing a majority.

The latest Channel 13 poll, published last week, captured that deadlock: Jewish Israeli parties opposed to Netanyahu were projected to win 52 seats, against 51 for the prime minister’s bloc, with both falling short of the 61 required for a majority.

Eisenkot’s Yashar party topped the poll with 22 seats, while Netanyahu’s Likud was projected to take 18. The lack of clarity over the next government – with both main blocs on the right – is fuelling unease among Israelis, some of whom believe little will change whoever becomes prime minister.

“I’m not going to vote because I don’t trust anyone,” said Rachel, 42, an Israeli citizen living in West Jerusalem. “I used to vote for Yair Lapid,” she added, referring to the leader of the centrist Yesh Atid party. “The party’s name means ‘there is a future’. But today, I don’t see any future for this country.”
Average public trust across the eight Israeli institutions measured consistently by the Israel Democracy Institute, a statistics body, stood at 34% in 2025, compared with 61% in 2012.

An atmosphere of pessimism and indecision is palpable in Jerusalem, where tensions between Palestinians in occupied East Jerusalem – the majority of whom cannot vote in Israeli national elections – and rightwing Jewish Israelis have deepened since 7 October. The Hamas attack is likely to weigh heavily on the ballot: a recent poll by the Israel Democracy Institute found that 68% of Jewish respondents said 7 October would be a central factor in deciding how they voted.

“After 7 October, everyone in this government has to take the blame,” said Ilda, who owns a clothing shop on Jaffa Street, one of Jerusalem’s oldest and busiest thoroughfares. Referring to a Haaretz investigation claiming Netanyahu had been warned about the possibility of a major Hamas attack, which he denies, she said: “After journalists exposed what happened, look what they did: they attacked the journalists instead of taking responsibility.”

West Jerusalem has long been considered fertile ground for Netanyahu and the Israeli right. Yet Israel’s growing diplomatic isolation and the prospect of seemingly endless conflict on multiple fronts are beginning to worry voters even here, a few steps from the bustling Mahane Yehuda market, where giant election posters for Itamar Ben-Gvir, the far-right national security minister known for his anti-Palestinian rhetoric and championing a racist death penalty law that in practice applies only to Palestinians, loom over the streets.

blocks.caption: Another advert showing Ben-Gvir at the Machane Yehuda market in Jerusalem.  Photograph: Quique Kierszenbaum/The Guardian

blocks.text: “This country needs radical change. I think I’ll vote for Naftali Bennett,” said Yosef, 26, a religious Israeli, referring to the rightwing former prime minister who now leads the B’Yachad alliance and is one of Netanyahu’s main political rivals.

On one side are tens of thousands of Netanyahu supporters – called “Bibi-ists” in reference to the prime minister’s nickname – as well as backers of the far-right ministers Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who want to return the current coalition to power to “finish the job” in Gaza, Iran, Lebanon and the West Bank.

On the other are tens of thousands of voters who believe Israel is losing its standing in the world and needs a change of direction – something many see as embodied by the centre-right Eisenkot. His supporters argue that he would place greater emphasis on education, social policy and the economy, areas they say have been neglected by the current government.

“I’ll vote for anyone but the prime minister of 7 October,” said Turgeman as he enjoyed a coffee with his wife at a cafe in Jaffa during the Jewish high holiday season. “I’ve never voted Likud in my life, and I’m certainly not going to start now. I’ll vote for Eisenkot. We need a normal prime minister – someone who also cares about the economy and about prices, which have soared because of the war.”

Food prices in Israel have reached record highs amid the regional conflict and supply chain disruption, with food inflation outpacing the broader consumer price index. The cost of food, including fresh fruit and vegetables, has risen by 9.5% over the past two years.

“They think about wars, while nobody is dealing with the economic crisis,” Turgeman said. “And what has Netanyahu done? He has continued to provide financial support that benefits the Haredi [ultra-Orthodox] community.”

Since 7 October, Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community has been at the centre of a bitter dispute over military conscription. While most Jewish Israelis serve, Haredi men studying in religious seminaries have long been largely exempt.

In 2024, amid war and growing pressure on reservists, the supreme court ruled there was no legal basis to continue the exemption, fuelling anti-draft protests, roadblocks and clashes with police. Haredi parties have blamed Netanyahu for failing to pass legislation to protect the exemption.

Ultra-Orthodox Jews, who make up about 14% of Israel’s population, have traditionally voted for parties backed by their rabbis, including the two main Haredi parties in Netanyahu’s coalition. But anger among younger Haredim over conscription and the policing of protests could lead some to defy their religious leaders this time.

“All the options in this election are junk, but I think I will vote for Eisenkot,” said Pinchas, 24, an ultra-Orthodox student who recently completed his military service. “I have the impression that this time people my age won’t vote according to what the rabbis tell them. Many are angry about the way Netanyahu handled the conscription law, and especially about the crackdown on those who protested against it.”

As the Guardian conducted interviews near Jerusalem’s central bus station, an elderly passerby called out: “There is only one prime minister – Bibi!” It was a reminder that, despite the uncertainty and the opposition’s narrow lead in the polls, the Israeli leader retains a loyal base.

blocks.caption: An advert for Gadi Eisenkot, a retired chief of staff of the Israeli army, on a bus in Jerusalem. Photograph: Quique Kierszenbaum/The Guardian

blocks.text: “I’m sure Netanyahu will win,” said Avraham Levy, 76, a Likud supporter and fruit seller at Mahane Yehuda market. “We’ll have the majority. We need to support Netanyahu because he has to finish the job. If he doesn’t, who will?” he said, referring to Israel’s wars on several fronts.

Among those still backing Netanyahu’s coalition partners are supporters of the far right, including Jakub, 23, who was due to begin his military service soon. “I’ll vote for Moshe Feiglin,” he said, referring to an extreme far-right former Israeli Knesset member who declared in 2025 that the conflict in Gaza was not against Hamas but against every child and baby in the territory, and is now running jointly with the far-right Religious Zionist party. “Because he represents my values, and he has never changed his principles,” Jakub said.

The field is wide open and the divide is also generational: by 2019, support for a Palestinian state stood at about 20%-30% among the youngest Jewish Israeli cohorts, compared with roughly 40%-55% among older generations, reflecting a longer-term shift towards more hawkish attitudes. No more recent comparable data was available.
The difficulty for the anti-Netanyahu camp is that it remains fragmented and has struggled to agree on a coherent political platform or a common strategy capable of uniting its different factions.

Parties representing Palestinian citizens, known as Arab parties inside Israel, could push Eisenkot’s coalition over the 61-seat threshold, but amid a campaign of racism and Islamophobia, he has ruled out going into government with them.
They could potentially support a minority government.

But last week, the Central Elections Committee voted to bar Ra’am and the Joint List, the country’s two main Palestinian parties, from the election, after the far-right Otzma Yehudit party filed a petition arguing that they support terrorism and deny the existence of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state.

The opposition Democrats party filed a similar petition arguing for Otzma Yehudit to be banned for incitement to racism and negating the existence of Israel as a democratic state, because of racist policies pursued in power under its leader Itamar Ben Gvir. That was not upheld.
The decision is being challenged in the supreme court, which has overturned similar bans in past elections.
If allowed to run in the elections, the Arab parties will be crucial to the opposition’s prospects of forming a government and to Eisenkot’s chances of replacing Netanyahu.

Tensions between Palestinian citizens of Israel and the state have deepened since 7 October amid arrests, interrogations and other legal action against Arab citizens, often over protests or social media posts.

blocks.caption: Avraham Levy at his fruit stall in the Mahane Yehuda market. Behind him is an image of Menachem Begin, a co-founder of the Likud party. Photograph: Quique Kierszenbaum/The Guardian

blocks.text: For these reasons, Palestinian citizens of Israel are often reluctant to express their voting preferences. In the 2025 Israeli Democracy Index survey, 70% said they preferred to remain silent about their political views in the presence of strangers, up from 45% in 2016 and compared with 53% of Jewish respondents.

But Palestinian citizens of Israel remain divided over how best to respond, with many pessimistic that any future government will defend rights they say have too often been denied. The Joint List has maintained a more oppositional stance, signalling it could support an anti-Netanyahu minority government from outside while stopping short of joining a coalition, although it has done so in the past.

“These elections are about our strength as an Arab community and our ability to have an influential political voice,” said Amir, 34, from Mashhad in northern Israel, who plans to vote for the Joint List. “We need strong, united Arab representation on equality, discrimination and the Palestinian cause, while cooperating when it benefits our community.”

Ra’am, led by Mansour Abbas, has instead made political pragmatism its defining strategy. In 2021 it became the first independent Arab party to join an Israeli governing coalition, seeking budgets, services and greater influence for Palestinian citizens of Israel.

“Arab society is being torn apart by crime and violence, while relations with Jewish Israelis are becoming more hostile,” said Abu Mahmoud, 33, from Kafr Kanna, also in the north of the country. “That’s why I’ll vote for Ra’am: negotiate, secure budgets and work with Jewish Israelis where possible.”
He added: “I want politics that can actually improve people’s lives.”
Jamal Risheq contributed to this report

articles.title: New Google Maps images reveal massive scale of devastation in Gaza
articles.summary:
Satellite imagery shows further destruction of homes, businesses and places of worship since fragile ceasefire

An update to Google Maps has revealed the extent of devastation during the…

blocks.text: An update to Google Maps has revealed the extent of devastation during the three-year Gaza war and the severity of the continuing humanitarian crisis faced by the territory’s 2.3 million inhabitants.
The images were taken in June this year and show further destruction of homes, businesses, places of worship and infrastructure since a fragile ceasefire came into effect almost 12 months ago.

blocks.caption: Gaza 2023-2026: al-Mawasi, Rafah

blocks.text: They show huge tented camps lining much of the shoreline, often within a few metres of the sea. Gaza’s once busy main port, now badly damaged and empty of fishing boats, is surrounded by makeshift accommodation. Any available open space in Gaza City is packed with shacks, tents and huts.

blocks.caption: Gaza 2023-2026: Tel al-Sultan, Rafah

blocks.text: The images also show massive damage to northern towns such as Beit Lahiya and Beit Hanoun, as well as the destruction of places of worship such as the Istiqlal mosque in Khan Younis. Major neighbourhoods in Gaza City such as Jabaliya and Shuja’iya, which were targeted in repeated Israeli offensives, are clearly now uninhabitable.

Swaths of rubble are visible in the south of Gaza, where a wide strip appears to have been cleared by Israeli forces along the border with Egypt. The town of Rafah appears to have been almost entirely reduced to rubble and Tel al-Sultan razed to the ground.

blocks.caption: Gaza 2023-2026: Istiqlal Mosque, Khan Younis

blocks.text: More than 2.1 million displaced people are living in tents and temporary shelters in Gaza, where about 82% of structures – roughly 200,000 buildings – have been damaged, with about two-thirds of those destroyed, according to the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, Unrwa.
A recent UN assessment estimated that the number of destroyed structures across Gaza had increased by 9% since the declaration of a ceasefire in October 2025.

blocks.caption: Gaza 2023-2026: Beit Lahiya

blocks.text: “The estimate of the total amount of rubble in Gaza is 61m tonnes. It is approximately 20 times the amount of rubble generated in all wars across the world over the last 18 years,” Jaco Cilliers, the UN Development Programme’s special representative in Palestine told the Guardian last month. The presence of human remains still buried under the rubble remains one of the most urgent humanitarian problems.

More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the start of the war, mostly civilians. The conflict was triggered by a surprise attack by Hamas into Israel in October 2023, in which militants killed about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and took 251 others hostage.

articles.title: ‘Explosion of melt rates’: 20% of Swiss glaciers lost in five years
articles.summary:
Alpine regions in Europe experiencing extreme glacier collapse due to heat-trapping effects of fossil fuel pollution

Switzerland has lost almost one-fifth of its ice in just five years,…

blocks.text: Switzerland has lost almost one-fifth of its ice in just five years, research has found, in a dramatic reshaping of the Alpine country whose big white glaciers have been reduced to moonlike rock deserts, scientists say.

Swiss glaciers shrank by 5.5% in the first eight months of 2026, according to an annual monitoring report, after a summer of scorching heatwaves that followed a winter with little snow. The reduction in ice volume falls just shy of the record set in 2022 and brings the total loss of glacier ice since 2021 to 19.4%.

blocks.caption: Glaciologist Matthias Huss records changes in the Scex Rouge glacier above Les Diablerets, western Switzerland. Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: Matthias Huss, a glaciologist at ETH Zürich and lead author of the report, said many people do not realise how fast glaciers are retreating, or that just one generation ago some now-barren sites used to sit beneath hundreds of metres of ice. The scientists have not yet compiled a formal tally of lost glaciers this year but said they had witnessed the death of a number of small ones.

“I visited one last week and it’s so impressive to stand in this moonlike landscape where there was a big layer of ice – an extensive glacier – just a few years ago,” said Huss. “And now it’s a rock desert where there’s some scattered blocks of old ice still lying around and melting on the hot rocks.”

The report, a collaboration between the Swiss Glacier Monitoring Network and the Swiss Commission for Cryosphere Observation, found the mean thickness of individual glaciers fell by between 2.5 metres and 4 metres in 2026. Huss said scientists were increasingly seeing glaciers collapse from the inside – the result of internal streams beneath the ice that excavate caverns – rather than simply retreating from surface heat.

blocks.caption: Matthias Huss looks at the ice on the Rhône glacier in Obergoms, Switzerland. Photograph: Pierre Albouy/Reuters

blocks.text: “You have huge holes like cheese in the middle of the ice that have collapsing roofs,” said Huss. “These are processes that tear the glaciers apart and make them retreat even faster.”

Europe is warming twice as fast as the global average from the heat-trapping effects of fossil fuel pollution and the destruction of nature, with Alpine regions experiencing some of the most dramatic changes.

Analysis published by MeteoSwiss on Tuesday found the summer half-year from April to September was the hottest and driest it had been since records began in 1864. In that time, humanity has filled the atmosphere with 1.8tn tons of carbon dioxide and heated the planet by about 1.4C.

The heat this summer was worse than in 2022 but Swiss ice loss just missed the record-breaking levels set that year. The scientists attributed this to limited deposits of Saharan dust, which foul the snow and prevent it from reflecting sunlight, as well as slightly greater snow cover at the end of winter and more sunlight in the summer.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Two mountaineers hiking on the Rhône Glacier, above Gletsch, in the Swiss Alps. Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: Huss visited the former Plattalvafirn, or Griess glacier, in September, which used to cover a mountain flank but lost 99% of its area in just 20 years. The glacier was the subject of some of the most detailed monitoring in the world in the 1950s and Huss worked with its data when he was a PhD student.

“What was different at that time, is that the rates of retreat were still kind of at a normal level,” said Huss. “What we are seeing now is a complete explosion of these melt rates, leading to the disintegration of glaciers. They’re really just falling apart.”

articles.title: Kyiv Independent editor: ‘Our readers want Russia to suffer but we can’t be propagandists’
articles.summary:
Olga Rudenko says news site has duty to report on Russian military gains and Ukrainian corruption even if subjects are not so well read

Readers of Ukraine’s leading English news site “really…

blocks.text: Readers of Ukraine’s leading English news site “really want Russia to suffer” but that should not lead the title to downplay the military and political problems facing Kyiv, its editor has said.

Speaking to the Guardian before an event to London, Olga Rudenko said many of the Kyiv Independent’s most-read stories described Ukrainian deep strike attacks into Russia, potentially distorting its coverage.

The Kyiv Independent, however, cannot afford to become propagandistic, she argued, and marginalise Russian military successes or reduce reporting on Ukrainian corruption because the subjects are not so well read.
“We had a conversation in the newsroom when somebody raised that our website, in the mornings, is all about Ukrainian attacks on Russian Wildberries warehouses and so on,” Rudenko said.
“But it’s misrepresenting the full picture when you don’t balance it out with enough stories about attacks on Ukraine, which are, by the way, far less popular with our readers.”
The challenge is that “people really want Russia to suffer”, and read about “something going boom” but it was the Kyiv Independent’s duty to “not just to feed them more of what they like”.

blocks.caption: Olga Rudenko: ‘It’s misrepresenting the full picture when you don’t balance it out with enough stories about attacks on Ukraine.’ Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

blocks.text: The “core idea of the Kyiv Independent is that we’re not Ukrainian propaganda, we’re not affiliated with the government, we’re not doing we’re not Ukraine’s PR service,” the editor said.

Rudenko said she had “no expectation” that the war would end any time soon, with Russia stepping up its bombing of Kyiv before winter and Ukrainian strikes denting its neighbour’s economy while diplomacy is stalled.

It is a feeling that has hung over journalists at the site for some time. This year employees did not bother planning for a peacetime scenario in their annual strategy session. “It was the first time when this question wasn’t really arising,” Rudenko said.

On Friday, Rudenko will host a “live story-telling event” in London where reporters, including the frontline correspondent Francis Farrell, will give their personal experience of Ukraine in the midst of the biggest war in Europe since 1945.

The title relies on readers to make monthly contributions for its revenue, an idea also used by the Guardian, and London was chosen as a venue because it “is probably the biggest city in terms of membership”, the editor said.

Media freedom in Ukraine has not worsened under Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Rudenko said, but added: “I would struggle to say it has gotten better.” Reporters can write freely without “fearing some immediate consequences” but the editor said that a concentration of power around the president remains.

Zelenskyy has not held a press conference for independent Ukrainian media since February 2025, and there is still a bitter legacy from the president’s attempt a few months later to neutralise Ukraine’s two anti-corruption agencies, which had to be reversed in the light of public protests.
after newsletter promotion

“We’ve been casting a critical look at Zelenskyy and his government for a while now, she said, highlighting an editorial written last July at the height of crisis, headlined “Zelenskyy just betrayed Ukraine’s democracy”.

The president and his allies, Rudenko said, had “brazenly and stupidly” sought to take away a central achievement of the Ukrainian revolution of 2014, after which the independence of Ukraine’s anti-corruption bodies was introduced.

Despite this, she said, “a critical mass of Ukrainians” do not think it is time to hold a presidential election, as called for by the former defence minister Mykhalio Fedorov in August. Elections have been suspended under martial law, though Zelenskyy’s term expired more than two years ago.

The Kyiv Independent has not come out in support of elections, Rudenko said, partly because support for holding them is running at about 15%. Protests this summer against Fedorov’s firing by Zelenskyy were “of the size that the president can still afford to ignore”, she added.
The Kyiv Independent was founded three months before the full-scale Russian invasion by journalists who had lost their jobs when the rival Kyiv Post was temporarily closed by its owner.
Launched with a $100,000 grant, it rapidly became an essential English language news sources for Ukraine as the country was attacked and the war with Russia became global news.

The number of contributing readers, or members, most of whom pay $5 a month, has risen from 14,000 at the beginning of 2025 to 25,500 a year later and to 36,000 now, allowing staff numbers to grow to 99 and the title to move to bigger offices.

articles.title: Who is Kathy Baldonado?
articles.summary: Who is Kathy Baldonado?The Senate impeachment court on Thursday is expecting the appearance of two provincial government officers who will testify on the alleged properties of Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published October 1, 2026 11:57am

The Senate impeachment court on Thursday is expecting the appearance of two provincial government officers who will testify on the alleged properties of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.
On the 32nd day of the impeachment trial of the vice president, Kathy Florence Baldonado appeared before the impeachment court following a subpoena issued to her.
Baldonado is the Register Deeds IV in Davao City and may comment about Carpio's alleged property in Matina.
The Senate impeachment court is currently tackling Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which specifically alleges that the Vice President accumulated unexplained wealth.
LIVE UPDATES: Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial (October 1, 2026)
As a register of deeds, Baldonado explained that her role entails real registration and issuance of land titles.

“Ako po bilang register of deeds ay nagre-rehistro or nagtatala po ng mga instrumento, mga dokumento po, or kasulatan regarding po ng mga real properties…Kami po yung nagi-issue ng katibayan ng titulo, kami rin po yung nagtatago ng mga records kaugnay dito po,” said Baldonado.

(As the Register of Deeds, I register or record instruments, documents, or deeds regarding real properties… We are the ones who issue certificates of title, and we also keep the records related to these.)

Baldonado said that she was told to bring several documents with her, such as transfer certificate of title, deed of sale, real property tax clearance, official receipt of transfer tax, and tax declarations for land, among others.
“Sa naalala ko po, ang hinihingi po ay isang certified true copy at tatlong USB drive ng mga dokumentong hawak ko po,” she said.
(From what I recall, what was requested was one certified true copy and three USB drives containing the documents in my possession.)

The net worth of Duterte and her husband reached more than P98 million in 2025, an 11.46% increase from their 2024 net worth based on their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
GMA News Research found that the Duterte-Carpio couple declared a net worth of P98,656,131.20 in 2025. The net worth they declared in the prior year was P88 million.
On the other hand, their declared total assets were P122,797,727.20, which is a 24.72% increase from the P98 million in 2024. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Jesse Baird’s housemate did not know surfboard bags contained bodies when she took photo, court hears
articles.summary:
Housemate tells court she saw the bags oozing red liquid she assumed was furniture rust

Jesse Baird’s housemate didn’t know she was looking at bags with Baird and his partner’s dead bodies,…

blocks.text: Jesse Baird’s housemate didn’t know she was looking at bags with Baird and his partner’s dead bodies, when she took a photo of oozing surfboard covers the night of their alleged murders, a court has heard.

Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

Baird’s housemate, known to the court under the pseudonym Belinda Smith, said she returned home from work on the evening after the shootings and went out to the courtyard to check on her washing after a day of heavy rain.
There, she saw “two surfboard bags with a blue tarp over the top of them and red liquid”, she told the trial on Thursday.
Smith took a photo of the liquid and sent it to their other housemate, known to the court under the pseudonym Sarah King. The photo was shown to the jury on Thursday.
Asked what she thought the liquid was, Smith told the court she believed it was “rusted water from the outdoor furniture”.
Asked by crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC if Baird had ever spoken to her about surfing or if she had seen a surfboard in their house, she confirmed she had not.
“You had no reason to suspect there was anything else in those surfboard bags?” he asked.
Smith responded: “no”.

In early 2024, relations had soured between Baird and his two housemates after they asked him to move out so one of their friends could take their spot. Baird eventually agreed and told their house group chat he would be moving out on 20 February 2024 Baird and Davies were fatally shot on 19 February. But when Smith left for work on the morning of the 20th and saw Baird’s belongings had not been packed up, Smith sent a message to King that read: “I’m genuinely scared this dude isn’t moving out today”.
A message was then sent from Baird’s phone to their housemate group chat claiming he had hired someone to collect his things and that he “might be doing a road trip to Perth with my mates”.

Smith responded she was “confused” and asked him to have his room emptied because cleaners would be arriving the following day. A response from Baird’s phone asked what time the cleaners had been booked. Afterwards, a number of Baird’s items were removed from his room.
By 22 February, the surfboards had been cleared and the liquid was gone, Smith told the court.
Baird and Davies’ bodies were eventually found in two surfboard bags five days later on the fence line of a rural monastery in Bungonia.

The defence lawyer John Stratton SC said during his opening statement that Baird and Davies were fatally shot in “self-defence” after struggles with the policeman. Lamarre-Condon immediately began cleaning up the scene because he “panicked”, the jury was told.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

After this decision, at least three petitions were filed before the SC last month.

articles.title: Raffy Tulfo: Trillanes should take witness stand first ahead of AMLC
articles.summary: The prosecution panel should present former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura of the Anti…

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 11:17am

The prosecution panel should present former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV as a witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura of the Anti Money Laundering Council (AMLC), Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo said Thursday.
Tulfo made the manifestation since the Senate impeachment court is yet to issue a subpoena to Trillanes pending the prosecution’s decision on the sequence of presenting witnesses.

“Kung kukunin na witness si former Senator Trillanes, much better mauna na muna siya bago AMLC. Kasi iyong mga sasabihin niya, may kinalaman sa mga bank accounts na nakalap niya a long time ago. Kung meron siyang ibubulgar na bank accounts, mga pera, pumasok, labas sa [bank] accounts na nakuha niya sa kanyang source. After natin makausap si Trillanes, iko-confirm ng AMLC,” Tulfo said.

(If you are getting Trillanes as witness, he should take the witness stand first because his testimony will be on the bank accounts he was able to collate a long time ago. If he has anything to reveal on these bank accounts, the amounts that came in and out...after we talk to him, the AMLC can confirm it.)
“So, dapat mauna si Mr. Trillanes, then AMLC. Hindi po AMLC then Trillanes (So, Trillanes must come first, not AMLC then Trillanes),” he added.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said the prosecution should be allowed to make the decision after lunch as it earlier told the court.
Tulfo then went on to say that the prosecution should ensure that the witnesses they are fielding will give meritorious accounts on impeachment allegations.

“Make sure that your witnesses will provide clarity on the impeachment case. Meron kayong kinuha na pinagtatawan tuloy, nagpapacute lang habang nakikipag-usap sa witness na police, etcetera, Ingat kayo sa pagkuha ng mga witness at ingat kayo sa pagsasalang ng mga abogado ninyo,” Tulfo added.

It was House prosecutor Bel Zamora who questioned the Police Major Jerickson Sangalang, Records Division chief of the Philippine National Police Firearms and Explosives Office on the guns owned by the Vice President and her husband, Manases Carpio.
Zamora asked the police official if it was appropriate for the Vice President to have 22 guns, but it was objected upon by the defense for being speculative. The court ruled in favor of the defense.
House prosecutor Keith Flores of Bukidnon responded by saying that it will take due notice and consider the advice of the Senator-judge Tulfo. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: OCD monitoring Cagayan Valley, Calabarzon, Caraga as very strong El Niño looms
articles.summary: The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Thursday it is closely monitoring three regions in Luzon and Mindanao amid the threat of the very strong El Niño in the last quarter of 2026.

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 11:13am
The Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Thursday it is closely monitoring three regions in Luzon and Mindanao amid the threat of the very strong El Niño in the last quarter of 2026.
The agency said effects have been recorded in Caraga, Calabarzon, and Cagayan Valley. In total, the number of affected persons has reached nearly 304,000, bulk of whom are in Caraga.

"[Sa Caraga region], based on the reports nasa 256,000 plus persons ang apektado. Sa Region 2 naman, there are 47,500 plus persons at sa Calabarzon, may na-report po na 191," said OCD spokesperson Vicente Gregorio Tomas in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB.
(In the Caraga region, based on the reports, over 256,000 persons are affected. In Region 2, there are over 47,500 persons, and in Calabarzon, 191 have been reported.)
State weather bureau PAGASA said the El Niño phenomenon could last until March or even June.
About 40 provinces are expected to experience less rainfall. Once January 2027 comes, this number could surge to 80.
Other than the drier weather, temperatures are also expected to rise from the minimum of three degrees Celsius to 38.7 degrees Celsius.

"Katuwang natin ang mga local government units, nagkaroon na po ng response measures. Naka-alert na po sila. Pinaigting po 'yung monitoring sa mga areas na maapektuhan nitong very strong El Niño," said Tomas.

(In partnership with local government units, response measures are already in place. They are now on alert. Monitoring has been intensified in the areas that will be affected by this very strong El Niño.)
With the threat of prolonged drought, the OCD advised the public to save on water resources.
"Magtipid po tayo sa paggamit ng tubig... Kapag umulan, salukin po natin 'yung empty containers o mga used containers, basta malinis lang po at hindi stagnant water," said Tomas.
(Let us conserve water... When it rains, let us catch the rainwater in empty containers or used containers, as long as they are clean and not stagnant water.) — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Swiss glaciers lose more than 5% in ice volume in 2026
articles.summary: Over the last five years, Swiss glaciers have lost nearly 20% of their mass, and 2026 saw the second-biggest loss of glacier volume on record. Experts warn there could be no ice left in the next…

image.caption: Scientists have warned of the total loss of the Swiss glaciers in the coming yearsImage: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Glaciers in Switzerland have lost nearly 20% of their mass in five years, experts said Thursday.
The experts said Swiss glaciers are melting rapidly and this year saw the second-biggest drop on record due to unprecedented heat waves in Europe.
There was a drop of 5.5% of Swiss glaciers this year, the Glacier Monitoring in Switzerland (GLAMOS) network found in a new study.
GLAMOS warns of total glacier loss
According to the report, over the past five years, the Swiss glaciers have lost almost ​a fifth of their ice, warning that in the future it could threaten water supplies.
The report also raised questions about the long-term survival of Europe's ice fields.
"Alpine glaciers have no chance of surviving in the long term under such conditions," said GLAMOS chief Matthias Huss. "The glaciers this year have lost enormous quantities of ice."
Little winter snowfall and record summer temperatures led Huss to call 2026 "a catastrophic year."
Locals face uncertainty after Swiss Alps glacier collapse
"This is a glacier that isn't surviving," he said. "There will probably be no ice in 10 or maybe 15 years."
The GLAMOS report reiterates concerns about the impact of global warming, especially in Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent.

"The warming that we are experiencing now can be attributed 100% to anthropogenic climate change. It's as simple as that," Huss said, using the term for climate change caused by human activity. "Without human emissions or fossil fuels we wouldn't have any warming at the moment."

articles.title: TBS: Don't generalize members as criminals
articles.summary: True Brown Style (TBS) Worldwide on Thursday urged authorities not to generalize or treat all members as criminals amid the government's crackdown against its organization.

blocks.text: Published October 1, 2026 11:12am
True Brown Style (TBS) Worldwide on Thursday urged authorities not to generalize or treat all members as criminals amid the government's crackdown against its organization.
“HUWAG LAHATIN. Hindi lahat ng may TBS sa pangalan, kulay, o affiliation ay kriminal. Hindi lahat ng TBS members pare-pareho ang ginagawa,” TBS Worldwide said in a Facebook post.
(DO NOT GENERALIZE. Not everyone with TBS in their name, color, or affiliation is a criminal. Not all TBS members do the same thing.)
“Marami sa amin ay professionals, workers, parents, business owners, at ordinaryong mamamayang sumusunod sa batas,” it added.
(Many of us are professionals, workers, parents, business owners, and ordinary law-abiding citizens.)
According to the group, some TBS members even help their communities and support people in need.
TBS Worldwide acknowledged that authorities have a responsibility to pursue individuals involved in criminal activities, particularly those involving minors.
The group called on authorities to hold accountable those who commit crimes, while ensuring that allegations are backed by evidence and involved persons are given due process.

“Kung may kriminal — hulihin ang kriminal. Kung may ebidensya — ilabas ang ebidensya. Kung may paglabag — panagutin ang lumabag. Pero huwag gawing dahilan ang ilang alegasyon para husgahan ang isang buong community,” TBS Worldwide said.

(If there is a criminal — catch the criminal. If there is evidence — release the evidence. If there is a violation — hold the violator accountable. But don't use a few allegations as a reason to judge an entire community.)
“WE DON'T ASK FOR SPECIAL TREATMENT. WE ASK FOR FAIR TREATMENT. Hindi kami humihingi ng proteksyon sa batas. Respeto at due process lang,” it added.
(WE DON'T ASK FOR SPECIAL TREATMENT. WE ASK FOR FAIR TREATMENT. We are not asking for protection from the law. Just respect and due process.)

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Wednesday said members of the community-based criminal gang TBS have established a presence in all local government units (LGUs) in Metro Manila and in 78 provinces.
EXPLAINER: Where did the TBS gang come from?
Remulla described cases involving TBS as extremely alarming that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered authorities to dismantle the organization.

According to authorities, the group is composed largely of members in their late teens and early 20s and also recruits children as young as 14 to 15 years old and grooms them for criminal activities. Initiation rites for new members may include robbing convenience stores at gunpoint. —VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: The ShinyHunters group says on September 22 it had stolen data ;on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job'

items: ShinyHunters, a cyber extortion group, claimed responsibility for hacking thousands of FBI agents' personal data and set a deadline for the FBI to retract a statement about them, after which their website went offline.
The stolen data reportedly included sensitive personal information about FBI agents and job applicants, and the group stated they had no intention of publishing the data.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The website used by ShinyHunters, the group that claimed responsibility for a recent hack of thousands of FBI agents’ personal and sensitive data, went offline on Wednesday, September 30, a day after the group’s deadline for the FBI to retract or modify a statement about the group’s tactics and track record expired.

ShinyHunters, a prolific cyber extortion group with a long record of targeting major corporations around the world, told Reuters and other news organizations on September 22 that it had stolen data “on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”

A Reuters analysis of a sample of the data shared by the hackers subsequently revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information.

Reuters could not determine why the site was offline. ShinyHunters could not be reached for comment.The hackers said they targeted the FBI in response to a May 2026 FBI advisory about the group that the hackers felt misrepresented their prior actions. They gave the FBI a week to either “correct or simply REMOVE” the advisory.
The advisory remains online. ShinyHunters later said it had no intention of publishing the data it stole and that it accomplished its goals.

The FBI said on September 23 that it was “actively and aggressively investigating” the breach. The agency declined to comment on Wednesday on whether it had taken any actions to force the hackers’ site offline. Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, urged the hackers in a video published on the agency’s website on September 29 to get in touch with the FBI “while the choice is still yours.”

Dutch police announced this week that on September 15 they had arrested a Dutch man in connection with an investigation into ShinyHunters. The hacking group told Reuters the man had “no association” with them and mocked the Dutch police as “incompetent.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Dennis Uy loses Donatela resort after foreclosure, another blow to shrinking empire
articles.summary: The luxury Bohol resort has been turned over to Landbank as Dennis Uy’s company struggles to overcome its overwhelming debt burden

blocks.text: LUXURY. A promotional image of Donatela Resort's Pool Villa.
Donatela Resort website
The luxury Bohol resort has been turned over to Landbank as Dennis Uy’s company struggles to overcome its overwhelming debt burden

items: Dennis Uy's luxury Donatela Resort and Sanctuary in Panglao, Bohol, has permanently closed following foreclosure due to unsustainable debt.
The resort, which catered to high-end travelers, was part of PH Resorts Group Holdings' broader restructuring efforts amid significant financial losses and liabilities.
PHR's financial struggles are highlighted by negative stockholders' equity and a substantial net loss, further complicating Uy's ambitious expansion during the Duterte administration.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Dennis Uy’s luxury Donatela Resort and Sanctuary in Panglao, Bohol, has permanently closed after the property was foreclosed, marking another retreat for the businessman whose debt-fueled empire expanded rapidly during the Duterte administration.
PH Resorts Group Holdings (PHR) disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary, Donatela Hotel Panglao Corporation, permanently ceased operating the resort at the end of September 30.

Donatela Resort and Sanctuary was an exclusive luxury retreat in Panglao, Bohol, set on a sprawling tropical estate with private villas, landscaped gardens, a spa, and a cliffside restaurant overlooking the sea. The boutique resort catered to high-end travelers seeking privacy and seclusion.
The problem was all that luxury was built on debt that Uy’s company was never able to meet.

The land and improvements comprising the hotel had been mortgaged to United Coconut Planters Bank, which has since been absorbed by Land Bank of the Philippines, and were subjected to extrajudicial foreclosure proceedings. Donatela was to turn over possession of the property to Landbank by the end of September.

Donatela was considerably smaller than Uy’s failed flagship Emerald Bay casino project, but it still represented a sizable chunk of what remained of PHR’s asset base. The land, buildings, and other improvements pledged to Landbank for the Donatela loan had a carrying value of about P1.44 billion as of June 2026, about half of PHR’s P2.79 billion in total consolidated assets.

Its closure comes as PHR attempts a much broader restructuring of a business hollowed out by years of losses and liabilities. Just a week earlier, in a September 23 disclosure, PHR laid out plans to transfer its stake in PH Travel and Leisure Holdings – through which it owns Donatela and its other operating subsidiaries – back to parent Udenna Corporation.

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] The rise and fall of Dennis Uy

blocks.text: “The Board determined that a comprehensive restructuring, involving the transfer of PH Travel to Udenna together with the rationalization of intercompany balances, offered the most direct and expeditious path to restoring PHR to a sustainable financial position, while providing a platform for future growth,” PHR said in its September 23 disclosure.

There is a lot of restoring to do. PHR’s consolidated stockholders’ equity was negative P5.953 billion as of June 30, while current liabilities exceeded current assets by around P4.01 billion. PHR is targeting a return to positive stockholders’ equity within two years after the restructuring. Restructuring, Uy’s company hoped, would remove most of the liabilities weighing on PHR and leave it operating largely as a listed holding company with no active business operations.

PHR’s 2025 financial statements show that strain clearly, with auditor SGV flagging a “material uncertainty” that could cast significant doubt on the parent company’s ability to continue as a going concern after it posted a P6.2-billion net loss, accumulated a P9.15-billion deficit, and recorded negative operating cash flow.

The Donatela foreclosure adds to the unraveling of the ambitions Uy built during the Duterte years. Uy, a major campaign donor of former president Rodrigo Duterte, snapped up everything from fuel, shipping, telecommunications, food, property, and gaming between 2016 to 2019. His meteoric rise drew scrutiny over his political ties to the administration, and the expansion itself leaned on borrowed capital.

Since then, PHR already lost control of the land and unfinished development behind its much larger Emerald Bay casino project in Cebu after its repurchase option expired in 2025, contributing to billions of pesos in losses. Its provisional gaming license was later revoked. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Google announces Gemini 4 flagship AI model after months of delays
articles.summary: The new AI model, 'Argon,'' is larger in size than Google's previous line of advanced "Pro" models, a company spokesperson says

blocks.text: GOOGLE. A Google logo is seen at a company research facility in Mountain View, California, U.S., May 13, 2025
Carlos Barria/Reuters
The new AI model, 'Argon,'' is larger in size than Google's previous line of advanced "Pro" models, a company spokesperson says

items: Google announced its new AI model 'Argon' as part of the Gemini 4 generation, aiming to compete with rivals Anthropic and OpenAI.
The model is larger and more performant than previous models, showing strong results on industry benchmarks, although it still lags behind in some coding metrics.
Google has decided not to release the previously planned Gemini 3.5 Pro and has undergone leadership changes in its AI lab amid delays in its AI model development.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

SAN FRANCISCO, USA – Alphabet’s Google on Wednesday, September 30, announced a new top-tier artificial intelligence model to anchor its Gemini 4 generation of models in a fresh bid to catch up to rivals Anthropic and OpenAI in the AI race.
The new model, “Argon,” is larger in size than Google’s previous line of advanced “Pro” models, a company spokesperson said.

“It’s our most performant model yet built for complex workloads, and we see it comparable to frontier models like (OpenAI’s) Astra and (Anthropic’s) Opus on key coding and cyber benchmarks,” the spokesperson said.

Google said it was providing the model to select cybersecurity partners and was participating in the Trump administration’s voluntary process for pre-release model access. It did not provide a timeline for the model’s public release.

The model posted better marks than Astra and Opus in terms of self-reported performance on several industry benchmarks, per a company press release. Still, Argon remained behind on certain other metrics, including two of the four coding-related benchmarks Google included in the release.
Google no longer plans to release Gemini 3.5 Pro, which CEO Sundar Pichai originally said would be released in June, according to the company spokesperson.
In the intervening time, Google overhauled its DeepMind AI lab, with its founder and CEO Demis Hassabis stepping aside and several leaders of its Gemini model leaving the company.
The months of delays to its AI model have caused the company to fall behind Anthropic and OpenAI, which continued to push the research frontier with new releases to its top models.

Pichai in July pushed back on the notion that Google was losing ground in the AI race. But Google in recent months has shifted its messaging from touting Gemini’s cutting-edge capabilities to highlighting its cost advantage compared to competitor models. – Rappler.com

With the rise in AI adoption, digital transformation, and demand for evolving strategic management skills, Mapúa University, in collaboration with Arizona State University (ASU), is expanding the Master of Business Administration (MBA) program with new industry-focused elective tracks under its E.T. “The Educational Management elective track is designed for professionals seeking leadership and management roles in educational institutions, while Healthcare Administration provides a pathway for professionals preparing to lead increasingly complex and technology-driven healthcare organizations,” Moreno explained.

The nine industry-focused elective tracks currently offered remain highly relevant to the demands of today’s rapidly evolving business landscape. The Financial Technology elective track continues to play a vital role in financial planning, investment management, and digital finance strategies for organizations operating in a global economy.

Likewise, the Digital Marketing with AI elective track reflects the growing integration of technology and data-driven information in brand management, customer engagement, and market analytics, enabling businesses to drive sustainable growth amid ongoing market transformations.
